newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ minister Henare rekindles talk of Maori party.
newsitem.headline: NZ minister Henare rekindles talk of Maori party.

text.p: Maori Affairs Minister and New Zealand First Party Deputy Leader Tau Henare has rekindled debate over the possibility of a new Maori party only days after his leader, Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters, ruled one out.
"There has been speculation of a Maori Party. You can't rule it in and you can't rule it out," Henare said in a newspaper interview that received widespread media coverage on Monday.
He said the party could be drawn from nationalist New Zealand First, or from the main opposition Labour Party, or even the left wing Alliance.
"It could be out of all three," he said.
NZ First is the junior partner in a centre-right coalition government formed around the conservative National Party.
Henare also praised free-market Act MP Donna Awatere-Huata.
"She's tops, and she shouldn't be languishing in Act." Unsurprisingly, he recommended she joined NZ First.
The minister said he would think about it if a group of MPs came to him suggesting he lead a Maori party. But he said he did not expect that to happen and had no wish to change now.
Last week Peters attacked the media for speculating there could be a Maori party formed, saying the reports were "patently false".
Peters declined to comment on Henare's interview on Monday. But NZ First president Doug Woolerton said there was no constituency for narrowly-based parties such as a Maori party.
NZ First won the balance of power in the October election and took centre stage in coalition talks prior to forming the government in December.
It won all five seats set aside for Maori, breaking Labour's long standing grip on the seats.
Henare, the MP for northern Maori seat Te Tai Tokerau, said despite polls showing Maori support returning to Labour, he was confident his party would hold all five in 1999.
But he did not rule out talking to Labour about a possible new coalition after that election.
"I would never, ever, ever again rule out governing with anybody as I did prior to the 1996 election," Henare said.
Last year Henare ruled out working in cabinet with Prime Minister Jim Bolger and other senior National ministers.
